name: 36952-codeedit-1.7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine, no sharding, no collectives.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=64, bounded at 640 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup 10% and cooldown 10%. Worst case 64 x 4360 tokens x 112 KiB = ~30 GB of KV, well inside one card.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over `configs/data/blazedit-96.jsonl`: 96 code-edit prompts pre-rendered from `vdaita/edit_5k_char` (train, all 96 rows), each a complete ~5.5k-character Python file plus a natural-language change request, in the Qwen3 chat template. 969 to 2360 prompt tokens, median 1442, mean 1467. Every request generates EXACTLY 2000 tokens (`output_tokens_count: 2000`, so `ignore_eos`). `temperature: 0.0`. The 640-request bound makes six and two-thirds passes over the 96 rows.
purpose: A code-editing assistant rewriting whole Python files from change requests, 64 concurrent long-output streams on one GPU.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B
speculative-config: {"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "prompt_lookup_min": 2, "prompt_lookup_max": 2}
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-num-seqs: 128
enable-chunked-prefill: true

# NOT this engine's default (it defaults to true), and off on purpose: the run is bounded at 640
# requests over a 96-prompt corpus, so with caching on every pass after the first would collapse to
# cache hits and the run would serve a different workload from the first pass onward.
enable-prefix-caching: false

max-model-len: 8192
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
